text:
Maria G: Hey team — customer 'FinShop' reporting intermittent 429s and says their dashboard shows quota left. They say it's only for a handful of keys. Sample response they pasted:

HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
x-rwi-rate-limit: 120; window=60; scope=org
x-rwi-remaining: 0
Request-Id: req_0a1b2c

They claim the app runs in a single project and only uses one API key. Can we triage?

Raj P: Thanks Maria. Quick Qs: are they behind a shared proxy or CDN? IP-based limits sometimes collide with org/project keys. Also which auth header are they sending?

Maria G: They say each client gets an API key (server-side) but frontends hit our public endpoint through a CDN (FastEdge). They pasted curl: `curl -H \"Authorization: Bearer sk-prod-XXXX\" https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate`

Leo T: Ok — two likely suspects: 1) org-level quota exhausted and per-key still shows quota in UI (UI can be eventual) OR 2) IP-scoped rule firing because CDN egress groups many clients under one IP. The header `x-rwi-rate-limit: 120; window=60; scope=org` suggests org-level enforcement.

Aria S: Can we get them to return the rate-limit headers for multiple requests? Also ask for `X-Forwarded-For` and the raw `Request-Id`. If proxying, rate meters may attribute to egress IP.

Maria G: Asked customer for X-Forwarded-For, Request-Id, example timestamps. They sent three entries: req_0a1b2c at 2024-05-09T14:02:12Z, req_0a1b2d at 14:02:33Z, req_0a1b2e at 14:03:01Z. They included `X-Forwarded-For: 54.23.12.34`

Raj P: Thanks. I'm seeing a pattern — bursts of 80 req/min from that IP in our infra logs attached to org_id=finshop-42. But our billing shows org commit not exceeded. I'll check project-level quotas and key mapping.

support-bot: Note: automated quota summary for org finshop-42: total quota 1,000,000 tokens/month, used 64%. Burst window tokens consumed in last hour: 92% of per-minute allowance.

Leo T: Important nuance: We have 3 layers of limits — key-level (strictest), project-level (aggregate of keys in a project), org-level (aggregate of projects and API usage), and IP-based emergency throttles. Precedence: IP emergency throttle can trigger even if key/project/org quotas are within allocated monthly commit. IP-based is applied to protect shared frontends.

Aria S: Another edgecase — if multiple projects share the same API key (misconfiguration) the key's usage might be higher than their UI per-project breakdown shows. Ask them to list keys bound to which project IDs.

Maria G: Customer confirmed one key is shared by two microservices across prod and staging. They will rotate; in meantime they asked for a temporary lift or bypass.

Raj P: Workaround steps we can offer: 1) If it's IP-based collision, recommend using routed egress or enable client-side token pinning so each client uses distinct key. 2) Create a project-scoped key for the heavy user. 3) If they need immediate relief we can open a short-lived burst allowance on their org (ops action). Need business justification and duration.

Maria G: They asked how we determine whether the 429 they saw was from IP limit vs org limit. Any quick signal?

Leo T: Look at the `scope=` value in `x-rwi-rate-limit` header. If `scope=ip` or contains `ip`, it's an IP rule. `scope=org` means org aggregated. Also check `x-rwi-bypass` header (if present) and `x-rwi-retry-after`. If header missing, sometimes middleware suppressed headers — ask for raw response capture.

support-bot: Tip: use `curl -i -H \"Authorization: Bearer <key>\" https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate` to include headers.

Maria G: Customer ran curl and sent back `x-rwi-rate-limit: 120; window=60; scope=ip:54.23.12.34` and `x-rwi-remaining: 0`. They also said billing-bot shows no overage.

Billing Bot: FYI — billing shows monthly tokens under commit. No auto-topup triggered. IP rules are independent of monthly commit.

Raj P: Given that, it's definitely IP-based. Options: 1) Ask customer to configure CDN to preserve client IP via `True-Client-IP` or pass client IP in `X-Forwarded-For` so we can differentiate. 2) Issue per-key rate limit increases (not ideal). 3) We can add an exception for their egress IP range for short period (Ops).

Aria S: For long-term, recommend application-level change: move token auth to backend so the RPS per egress IP drops, or shard requests across multiple egress IPs. Also add instrumentation: emit `Request-Id` and store headers so we can debug future incidents.

Ops Oncall: I can open a temporary IP-exception for 4 hours once we have the customer's legal ack. Provide target IP(s) + org id. I'll need requestor + reason.

Maria G: I'll collect the signed ack and the IP list. Meanwhile the customer asked how to reproduce locally since their dev env doesn't hit the CDN. Any reproducible steps?

Leo T: Repro steps: run a tight loop hitting their API key from one IP until you see `x-rwi-remaining: 0`. Example script:
```bash
for i in {1..200}; do curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} %{time_total}\n" -H \"Authorization: Bearer sk-prod-XXXX\" https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate; sleep 0.2; done
```
That mimics bursts and will trigger IP or key limits depending on which is hit first.

Maria G: Great. Customer rotated keys and will move to per-service keys. They also requested that we add a note to their org settings explaining IP vs org vs key precedence. Could be helpful in UI.

Raj P: I'll file a product request. For now logging ticket SR-5891 to provision a 4-hour exception once ops gets ack.

Maria G: Thanks everyone — marking thread follow-up. Will post updates when customer sends ack. :thumbsup:
